batch_node.name: okta: org page v0.1.0
batch_node.description: The /okta page (req-okta-page-org): one page, a graph panel over a projection with the okta-org.js layout and its org-scoped scene searches, and fifteen standard table panels, each over one org-scoped search. Every search takes ?org=<org name>; nothing here names an org or an entity id outside this bundle.

node.name: Okta
node.description: One Okta org as a FedRAMP operator reads it: the configuration as a picture (applications, groups, policies, authenticators, federation, administration), then the tables an assessor asks about first: who is assigned what, who holds admin roles, which sign-on rules demand which factors, users who are not active or not signing in, API tokens, network zones, trusted origins and where the System Log goes. ?org=<org name> picks the org (exact match); absent, every org on the grid is shown (the one org, on a single-org grid). Every search that joins two Okta objects scopes both to the org.

node.name: okta — the org
node.description: The org node itself, so an org with nothing in it yet still draws. Scene search for the /okta graph panel.

org.description: The Okta org's name (okta__okta_org.name, its natural key), from ?org= on the page, matched exactly. Absent, the default is the sentinel 'okta__okta_org' (the org type's own slug), which every org's entity_type equals, so every org matches: the one org on a single-org grid. The sentinel stands in for the optional filter Gryphon cannot yet say directly (tap#360); an org literally named 'okta__okta_org' would read as every org.

node.name: okta org layout
node.description: Draws one Okta org at the centre of a 3x3 grid of family boxes (Federation, Authenticators, Network above; Groups left and Applications right; Administration, Policies below), each policy's rules nested inside it. Names no entity id: reusable for any org, and a node whose type no family names is drawn in an Other box and reported.

node.name: okta org elevation
node.description: One Okta org at one elevation.

definition.description: One Okta org at one elevation.

node.name: okta org projection
node.description: The /okta graph: one elevation, one layout module (okta-org.js). Icon-badge node style; placement fixed (lock_nodes); opens fitted.

node.name: Okta org
node.description: The org's configuration in one picture: which groups are assigned which applications, which authentication policy each application is bound to and the authenticators its rules require, inbound federation, and who holds which admin role. Users, devices and API tokens are in the tables below.

node.name: okta — applications in the org
node.description: Every okta__okta_application that BELONGS_TO_ORG__okta the org. Envelope mode (RETURN n) so the table receives typed nodes; sorted client-side (Gryphon refuses ORDER BY on a traversal).

org.description: The Okta org's name (okta__okta_org.name, its natural key), from ?org= on the page, matched exactly. Absent, the default is the sentinel 'okta__okta_org' (the org type's own slug), which every org's entity_type equals, so every org matches: the one org on a single-org grid. The sentinel stands in for the optional filter Gryphon cannot yet say directly (tap#360); an org literally named 'okta__okta_org' would read as every org.

node.name: Applications
node.description: Every application integration in the org and how users sign in to it. SAML and OIDC federate; SWA (BROWSER_PLUGIN, AUTO_LOGIN, SECURE_PASSWORD_STORE) and BASIC_AUTH vault a password Okta replays, which a FedRAMP boundary usually has to justify. A blank cell is not observed, never 'none'.

columns.title: Application
columns.header_tooltip: The label users see on their dashboard.

columns.title: Sign-on mode
columns.header_tooltip: Okta's signOnMode. Amber: the app is signed in by a vaulted password, not a federated assertion.

columns.title: OAuth type
columns.header_tooltip: For OIDC and service apps: web, native, browser or service (client credentials, no user).

columns.title: Catalog key
columns.header_tooltip: Okta's app name: the integration-network key, or a generated key for a custom app.

columns.title: Client id
columns.header_tooltip: The OAuth client_id, for OIDC and service apps.

node.name: okta — application assignments
node.description: Each ASSIGNED_APPLICATION__okta edge between an assignee and an application that both BELONG_TO_ORG the org: the application, the assignee (a group or a user) and the edge's scope, priority and status. PROJECTION mode (rows, not nodes).

query: WHERE (o.data.name = $org OR o.entity_type = $org) AND (o2.data.name = $org OR o2.entity_type = $org)

RETURN a.data.label AS application, a.data.sign_on_mode AS sign_on_mode, p.name AS assignee, p.entity_type AS assignee_type, e.data.properties.scope AS scope, e.data.properties.priority AS priority, e.data.properties.status AS status, a.entity_id AS application_id

org.description: The Okta org's name (okta__okta_org.name, its natural key), from ?org= on the page, matched exactly. Absent, the default is the sentinel 'okta__okta_org' (the org type's own slug), which every org's entity_type equals, so every org matches: the one org on a single-org grid. The sentinel stands in for the optional filter Gryphon cannot yet say directly (tap#360); an org literally named 'okta__okta_org' would read as every org.

node.name: Who is assigned each application
node.description: One row per assignment: a group or a user assigned an application. A group assignment reaches every member; a user row scoped GROUP was inherited from one. Assignments are what put an application on a user's dashboard and let Okta issue an assertion for them.

columns.title: Assignee
columns.header_tooltip: The group or user it is assigned to.

columns.title: Scope
columns.header_tooltip: For a user: USER when assigned directly, GROUP when inherited from a group assignment. Blank for a group row.

columns.title: Priority
columns.header_tooltip: For a group: which group's app profile wins when several assign the same app.

columns.title: Sign-on mode
columns.header_tooltip: The application's signOnMode, repeated so the table reads on its own.

node.name: okta — admin role assignments
node.description: Each principal that HOLDS_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT__okta an assignment, the role it GRANTS_ADMIN_ROLE__okta; the holder and the role are both scoped to the org. PROJECTION mode. The assignment's scope is not joined: OPTIONAL MATCH v0 needs a single-node mandatory MATCH.

query: WHERE (o.data.name = $org OR o.entity_type = $org) AND (o2.data.name = $org OR o2.entity_type = $org)
RETURN p.name AS holder, p.entity_type AS holder_type, r.data.name AS role, r.data.role_type AS role_type, ra.data.assignment_type AS assignment_type, ra.data.status AS status

org.description: The Okta org's name (okta__okta_org.name, its natural key), from ?org= on the page, matched exactly. node.name: Admin role assignments
node.description: Who holds which administrator role. A group holding a role gives it to every member, which is why an admin role assigned to a group is only as tight as that group's membership. The scope of each assignment (resource set or target groups/apps; none means the whole org) is drawn on the graph above; Gryphon cannot yet join an optional scope into these rows.

columns.title: Holder
columns.header_tooltip: The user, group or service app holding the assignment.

columns.title: Kind
columns.header_tooltip: User, group or service app (a CLIENT assignment).

columns.title: Role type
columns.header_tooltip: Red: a role that can change who else is an administrator or reset anyone's factors.

columns.title: Assigned to
columns.header_tooltip: Okta's assignmentType: USER, GROUP or CLIENT.

entity.name: Sign-on rules and their factor requirement

node.name: Sign-on rules and their factor requirement
node.description: Every rule of every global session and authentication policy, in the order Okta evaluates them: whether it allows or denies, and whether it demands one factor type or two. A 1FA ALLOW rule is a password-only path in, and the catch-all rule at the bottom is the one that decides everything nobody wrote a rule for. Blank factor mode is not observed, never 'no MFA'.

columns.title: Policy
columns.header_tooltip: The policy the rule belongs to.

columns.title: Kind
columns.header_tooltip: Global session policy or authentication (app sign-on) policy.
Evaluation order within the policy (1 first).

columns.title: Access
columns.header_tooltip: What the rule decides when it matches.

columns.title: Factors
columns.header_tooltip: 2FA: two factor types required. 1FA: one is enough, which for an ALLOW rule means a password alone can pass.

columns.title: Re-verify after
columns.header_tooltip: ISO-8601 duration before the user must verify again.

node.name: okta — authenticators required by rules

node.name: Authenticators each rule requires

columns.title: Policy

columns.title: Authenticator
columns.header_tooltip: The authenticator that satisfies the rule.

columns.title: Constraint

columns.title: Phishing-resistant

node.name: API tokens
node.description: Okta API tokens: long-lived secrets that act with the admin permissions of the user who created them, at the moment of each call. A token that can be used from anywhere, belonging to a super administrator, is a standing super-admin credential. Who each token acts as is its ACTS_AS_USER edge; Gryphon cannot yet join an optional owner into this row.

columns.title: Expires
